userStories.title: Add @refresh reset directive to RunViewPanel and PipelineMonitorPanel
userStories.description: Both RunViewPanel.tsx and PipelineMonitorPanel.tsx call useWorkspace() at the top of their component bodies but lack the `// @refresh reset` Vite HMR directive that SpecsPanel.tsx already has. During hot module replacement, React hook state can desync from the WorkspaceProvider tree, causing an intermittent 'useWorkspace must be inside WorkspaceProvider' error caught by the ErrorBoundary labeled 'Runs'. The user must click Retry to recover. Fix: add `// @refresh reset` as the very first line (before all imports) in both src/panels/RunViewPanel.tsx and src/panels/PipelineMonitorPanel.tsx.
acceptanceCriteria: The string `// @refresh reset` appears as the very first line of src/panels/RunViewPanel.tsx, before any import statements
The string `// @refresh reset` appears as the very first line of src/panels/PipelineMonitorPanel.tsx, before any import statements
Both files pass `npx tsc --noEmit` with no new type errors
After a simulated HMR update (edit and save either file), no 'useWorkspace must be inside WorkspaceProvider' error appears in the browser console or ErrorBoundary

userStories.title: Extract usePipelineRuns shared hook to eliminate duplicate polling and 429 storms
userStories.description: Two independent polling intervals hit GET /api/pipeline/runs simultaneously: AppLayout (src/App.tsx ~line 403) polls every 10s for the sidebar active-run badge, and PipelineMonitorPanel polls the same endpoint every 15s for the run list. When the ErrorBoundary retries after the HMR crash (Bug 1), both restart simultaneously, generating a burst exceeding the 100 req/min rate limiter and causing 429 responses that cascade into a retry storm. Fix: create src/hooks/usePipelineRuns.ts that uses a module-level singleton cache (ref + timestamp) to deduplicate in-flight requests. Both AppLayout and PipelineMonitorPanel must be refactored to consume this hook instead of their own fetch intervals. Only one HTTP request should be in-flight at any given time regardless of how many components are subscribed.
acceptanceCriteria: A new file src/hooks/usePipelineRuns.ts exists and exports a usePipelineRuns hook that accepts an optional polling interval parameter
The hook uses a module-level cache (e.g., a Map or singleton ref) so that concurrent subscribers share a single in-flight request and a single polling interval
src/App.tsx no longer contains its own setInterval or useEffect polling block for /api/pipeline/runs — it imports and calls usePipelineRuns instead
src/panels/PipelineMonitorPanel.tsx no longer contains its own polling block for /api/pipeline/runs — it imports and calls usePipelineRuns instead

Opening both AppLayout and PipelineMonitorPanel simultaneously results in at most one outstanding fetch to /api/pipeline/runs at any given time (verifiable via browser Network tab or a unit test that mocks fetch and counts calls)
Both frontend and backend pass `npx tsc --noEmit` with no new type errors

userStories.title: Emit run_setup_started and run_setup_done WAL events from execution-engine during wave worktree creation
userStories.description: When wave parallel execution is enabled, execution-engine.ts creates git worktrees for every story in wave 0 before spawning any agents (N × `git worktree add`, ~3–5s each for large specs). During this phase the terminal is blank, no WAL events are emitted, and the UI appears frozen. Fix: in backend/src/lib/execution-engine.ts, emit a WAL event with event_type 'run_setup_started' and payload { phase: 'worktree_creation', wave: 0, story_count: N } immediately before the worktree creation loop begins, and emit 'run_setup_done' with payload { phase: 'worktree_creation', wave: 0, story_count: N } immediately after all worktrees are created. Both events must include run_id, workspace_id, and spec_id in their payload to match the standard WAL event contract used by other events in the engine.
acceptanceCriteria: execution-engine.ts emits a WAL event with event_type='run_setup_started' and payload.phase='worktree_creation' before the first `git worktree add` call in wave-parallel mode
execution-engine.ts emits a WAL event with event_type='run_setup_done' and payload.phase='worktree_creation' after the last `git worktree add` call completes successfully
Both WAL events include run_id, workspace_id, spec_id, and story_count in their payload
WAL events are NOT emitted when running in sequential (non-wave) mode
Backend passes `npx tsc --noEmit` with no new type errors after the changes

userStories.title: Show wave setup banner in RunViewPanel during worktree creation phase
userStories.description: RunViewPanel.tsx has no awareness of the pre-story setup phase during wave parallel runs. When run_setup_started arrives (from US-003) but no story_started has yet arrived, the terminal is blank and the run looks frozen. Fix: in src/panels/RunViewPanel.tsx, subscribe to the SSE WAL event stream and track a local isInSetupPhase boolean. Set it to true when event_type='run_setup_started' arrives; set it to false when event_type='run_setup_done' OR the first event_type='story_started' arrives. When isInSetupPhase is true, render a visible amber/blue banner above the terminal area reading 'Preparing N parallel worktrees…' (N taken from the WAL event payload.story_count). The banner must disappear as soon as setup is done and story execution begins.
acceptanceCriteria: RunViewPanel renders a setup banner containing the text 'Preparing' and the story count when event_type='run_setup_started' is received and no story_started event has yet arrived
The setup banner disappears when event_type='run_setup_done' is received
The setup banner disappears when the first event_type='story_started' is received (handles the case where run_setup_done is missed)
The banner is NOT shown for sequential (non-wave) runs where run_setup_started is never emitted
Frontend passes `npx tsc --noEmit` with no new type errors

userStories.title: Show simultaneous pulsing Running indicators and parallel count banner in RunStoryList for wave runs
userStories.description: When wave parallel execution is active with parallelism > 1, the story sidebar (RunStoryList or equivalent story list in RunViewPanel) only highlights the most recently started story, making it appear that only one story is running. MultiPaneTerminal exists and activates when 2+ story_started WAL events arrive, but the story list UX does not reflect the parallel reality. Fix: track all stories that have received story_started but no completion event (story_passed, story_failed, story_skipped) simultaneously in a Set of activeStoryIds. Render ALL entries in that Set with a pulsing green 'Running' indicator at the same time (not just the latest one). Additionally, when activeStoryIds.size > 1, show a banner above the terminal area reading 'N stories running in parallel' where N = activeStoryIds.size. Do NOT add story_id to run_output_chunks or attempt to split the terminal stream — that is deferred to a separate spec.
acceptanceCriteria: When 2 or more story_started WAL events have arrived without corresponding completion events, all N currently-running stories in the story list show a pulsing 'Running' indicator simultaneously
A banner reading 'N stories running in parallel' (where N >= 2) appears above the terminal when multiple stories are concurrently active
The banner and pulsing indicators disappear for a story as soon as its story_passed, story_failed, or story_skipped event arrives
In sequential runs (only one story active at a time), no parallel banner is shown and only the single active story shows the Running indicator
Frontend passes `npx tsc --noEmit` with no new type errors

=== GLOBAL STANDARDS (L1) ===
principles:
  typescript:
    strict_mode: true
    target: ES2022
    no_any: "Avoid `any` — use `unknown` with type guards or explicit generics"
    async_first: "All DB calls, LLM calls, and I/O are async — always await"

  error_handling:
    pattern: "AppError class hierarchy with immutable HTTP status codes"
    subclasses: [ValidationError 400, AuthError 401, ForbiddenError 403, NotFoundError 404, ConflictError 409, UnprocessableError 422]
    serialization: "{ error: string, code?: string, details?: Record<string, unknown> }"
    rule: "Throw from route handlers; centralized errorHandler middleware catches and serializes"

  database:
    driver: "pg Pool (async, connection pooling)"
    helpers: "query<T>() returns T[], queryOne<T>() returns T|undefined, execute() returns { rowCount }"
    placeholders: "$1, $2, ... (numbered, NOT positional ?)"
    transactions: "transaction<T>(fn) wraps in BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK"
    migrations: "SQL files in pg-migrations/, timestamp prefix YYYYMMDDHHMMSS for new files, tracked in schema_migrations"
    slow_query_logging: "Queries > 500ms logged with sanitized params"

  validation:
    library: zod
    pattern: "Middleware factories — validateBody(schema), validateQuery(schema), validateParams(schema)"
    method: "safeParse (not .parse() which throws)"
    response: "{ error: firstIssueMessage, details: zodError.issues }"

  llm:
    return_type: "ChatResult { text: string, usage: { inputTokens, outputTokens } }"
    rule: "Always use .text accessor — never treat ChatResult as a string"
    providers: "Multi-provider routing via model registry — claude-cli, anthropic, openai-compat, openrouter"

  api_design:
    documentation: "JSDoc @swagger annotations on every route → auto-generated OpenAPI spec"
    pagination: "{ items: T[], total: number, hasMore: boolean, cursor?: string }"
    response_shape: "Success: res.json(data). Error: { error, code, details } via AppError"
    middleware_chain: "validateBody(schema) → authRequired → async handler"
    security_headers: "helmet (CSP, HSTS, X-Frame-Options, noSniff, referrerPolicy)"
    caching: "Cache-Control: no-store on all responses, etag: false"

  testing:
    backend: "Jest with ts-jest, serial (maxWorkers: 1), 30s timeout, PG_POOL_SIZE=1"
    frontend: "Vitest with jsdom, globals: true"
    rule: "Always clean up DB pool connections in afterAll()"

  code_style:
    no_over_engineering: "Only make changes that are directly requested or clearly necessary"
    no_premature_abstraction: "Three similar lines > premature helper function"
    minimal_containers: "Don't add docstrings, comments, or type annotations to code you didn't change"
    security_first: "Never commit .env files, API keys, or secrets. Use vault for sensitive values."

=== PROJECT CONTEXT (L3) ===
name: rorca
type: web-app
purpose: AI spec orchestration platform that converts plain-English briefs into structured user story specs and autonomously executes them story-by-story via isolated agent subprocesses (claude, opencode, or codex)

stack:
  - React 18
  - TypeScript 5.7 (strict)
  - Vite 5
  - Tailwind CSS 3
  - xterm.js (@xterm/xterm)
  - react-router-dom 7
  - framer-motion
  - recharts
  - Express.js
  - PostgreSQL 16 (pg pool, pgvector, Apache AGE)
  - pg-boss (job queue)
  - Node.js >= 20
  - tsx (TypeScript runner)
  - Jest (backend tests)
  - Vitest (frontend tests)
  - Playwright (E2E)

key_modules:
  - src/panels/ — 5 primary UI panels (Specs, Runs, Analytics, Direction, Settings)
  - src/components/ — shared UI (Sidebar, RunTerminal, CommandPalette, slide-overs)
  - src/contexts/ — WorkspaceContext, AuthContext, ThemeContext, ToastContext
  - backend/src/routes/ — 32 Express route files
  - backend/src/lib/ — core services (sse-hub, direction-stack, llm-client, execution-engine, context-router, workspace-echolocation, rate-limiter, scheduler)
  - backend/src/worker.ts — pg-boss worker process (pipeline job consumer)
  - backend/src/lib/execution-engine.ts — sole execution engine for all agent types
  - backend/src/db/ — PostgreSQL pool, migration runner, 70+ migrations
  - backend/src/mcp/ — MCP stdio server (24 tools)
  - forge/ — spec JSON files, run-loop.sh bash fallback, self-register script

constraints:
  - Migrations must use timestamp format YYYYMMDDHHMMSS for new files (sequential 001-079 already exist)
  - Worker process must be running for pipeline triggers to execute
  - AGE search_path must be restored after every graph query
  - Auth middleware is globally disabled (intentional, local tool)
  - CLAUDE_BIN full path required for child process spawning (NVM PATH not inherited)
  - spec id is always the filename slug, never the human title

deployment_target: local (self-hosted, npm run dev) or Docker Compose

  frontend: 5210
  backend: 3030
  finops_sim: 5200

integrations:
  - claude CLI (claude --print)
  - opencode CLI (opencode run)
  - codex CLI (codex --approval-mode auto-edit)
  - GitHub OAuth + webhooks
  - Linear (post-launch)
  - Vercel (post-launch)
  - Slack (post-launch)

=== SPEC BRIEF (L4) ===
Fix four confirmed bugs in the Runs panel (src/panels/RunViewPanel.tsx and src/panels/PipelineMonitorPanel.tsx) that cause persistent UX failures in Rorca.

BUG 1 — useWorkspace HMR crash: RunViewPanel.tsx and PipelineMonitorPanel.tsx both call useWorkspace() at the top of their component bodies but lack the `// @refresh reset` Vite directive that SpecsPanel.tsx already has. This causes an intermittent "useWorkspace must be inside WorkspaceProvider" error caught by the ErrorBoundary with label "Runs", requiring the user to click Retry. Fix: add `// @refresh reset` as the very first line of both files.

BUG 2 — 429 rate-limit storm on /api/pipeline/runs: Two independent polling intervals hit the same endpoint simultaneously. AppLayout (src/App.tsx ~line 403) polls /api/pipeline/runs every 10s for the sidebar badge. PipelineMonitorPanel polls the same endpoint every 15s for the run list. When the ErrorBoundary retries (from Bug 1), both restart simultaneously, causing a burst that exceeds the 100 req/min rate limiter. Fix: extract a shared React hook (e.g. usePipelineRuns in src/hooks/) that deduplicates fetches via a module-level cache or ref, so only one in-flight request exists at a time regardless of how many components subscribe.

BUG 3 — Wave parallel 2-minute silent startup: When wave parallel execution is enabled, execution-engine.ts creates git worktrees for every story in wave 0 before spawning any agents (N × git worktree add, ~3–5s each). The UI shows no progress during this phase — the terminal is blank and the run appears frozen. Fix: execution-engine.ts should emit a WAL event (event_type: 'run_setup_started', payload: { phase: 'worktree_creation', wave: 0, story_count: N }) before worktree creation, and 'run_setup_done' after. RunViewPanel.tsx should show a setup banner ("Preparing N parallel worktrees…") when the run is in setup phase (after run_setup_started but before the first story_started WAL event).

BUG 4 — Wave parallel: concurrent stories invisible in terminal: run_output_chunks has no story_id column, so all parallel stories write to the same stream. MultiPaneTerminal exists and is wired (activates when 2+ story_started WAL events arrive) but the single stream cannot be split by story. Fix: in the RunStoryList / story sidebar, when a wave run is active with parallelism > 1, render all currently-running stories (story_started received, no completion event yet) with a pulsing "Running" indicator simultaneously — making clear that N stories are executing in parallel even though the terminal is unified. Also show a "N stories running in parallel" banner above the terminal when useMultiPane is true. Do NOT attempt to split the terminal stream (that requires a schema migration to add story_id to run_output_chunks, which is a separate spec).
